title: Thin walls thickened before the drawing is opened
summary: The drawing grows every section thinner than its opening keeps at every grid phase (1.75 mm on its 0.25 mm grid) where it can, with balls 1.7 mm across, then opens at 0.65 mm (surface_open_mm: half of C7's 1.26 mm wall and a hair over), sparing the 1.4 mm hub (geometry._thicken, geometry._open). It leaves the exact features' own sections alone: drawn() puts them back at their size. Over the props' discs it grows outward only within the plan the frame already covers there, and up and down where a ball does not fit, so it adds nothing to the shadow (14.6 %; C14 allows 15 %); nowhere does it grow further than 1 mm from the body as first drawn. What it grows are the sheets the field's grey top cell layer draws, 0.35 mm where they join the front and back limbs to the rim, and those the props' keep-out leaves of the layer under it, 0.47-0.61 mm under the guard arcs. On cad.wall_thickness's own ray from every face, all but 32 of about 320,000 faces read at least 1.26 mm: 8 slanted facets at the bottom edge of each seat's centre hole read 0.99 mm (the seat is 1.3 mm between its holes), 8 at the bottom corners of the guard arcs' ends 1.05-1.07 mm (the arc is 1.4 mm), 12 under the guard arcs 1.12-1.23 mm, and 4 at the hub's bottom edge by the side posts 1.19 mm. The gate's 4000 evenly spaced faces read 1.33 mm and miss them; a rebuild that moves its sample has about one chance in three of landing on one. The guards read 4.15 mm tall, as before (C13). The PETG frame is 17.03 g against 16.87 g before. The opening also takes about 480 mm^3 of the body as first drawn, in some 5,900 skims and fringes of at most 20 mm^3 (the largest are the field's fillets along the side bands).
